rationale: C09 plausibly supplied a material template for the child’s retirement tribute. Both letters move from acknowledging withdrawal or retirement, to praising distinguished leadership and service, to invoking the admiration or gratitude of the Free World, and finally to wishing the recipient a happy retirement. The unusually concentrated overlap in both structure and vocabulary is stronger than generic complimentary-letter boilerplate. C13 presents a similarly close retirement-tribute pattern, while C04 is a weaker resignation-letter analogue.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Your tenacity and indomitable courage ... won the admiration of the entire Free World as well as the gratitude of all Koreans.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The leadership and judgment which you have displayed ... has won the great admiration ... of all the Free World. ... you take with you the gratitude of the people of the United States
shared_material.explanation: Both pair admiration extending across the Free World with the gratitude of the recipient’s nation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: With your voluntary withdrawal from political life, I am reminded ever more strongly of how much your country will remain in your debt.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: At the same time, I do, of course, take note of the fact of your forthcoming retirement from the United States Navy. As you leave, you take with you the gratitude of the people of the United States
shared_material.explanation: Both use the occasion of a voluntary departure to emphasize the enduring national debt owed for past service.

shared_material.child_excerpt: My best wishes for many years of health and happiness in the honored retirement which you have done so much to earn.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: my very best wishes to you and Phyllis for a happy and rewarding retirement.
shared_material.explanation: The closing retirement wish is closely parallel in wording and function.
